title: Thin-client protoflows & API-surface guide (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures a lightweight, opinionated set of onboarding "protoflows" and the minimal API surface for a thin client that teams can embed into web/mobile apps. Aim is to propose a small, composable surface that gets customers from install -> first successful inference -> basic observability in under 10 minutes.

Audience:
- Product engineers who want a minimal integration path for Redwood API features (chat/generate/embeddings)
- SDK maintainers who will implement the thin client reference
- Solutions engineers who will ship sample apps and quick demos

Constraints and design goals (non-exhaustive):
- Keep surface tiny: ~4 top-level calls (init, send, receive/stream, teardown).
- Default to Redwood hosted API but allow explicit Dedicated/Private endpoint override in config.
- Minimal async complexity for host app: provide Promise and callback flavors plus a small streaming event emitter for progressive UX.
- Telemetry-lite only: emit a single handshake + outcome event (no heavy per-token telemetry by default).
- Offline-friendly: a deferred-local-cache mode for short interruptions and instant UI fallback.

High-level API surface (proposal):
1) rwinf.bootstrap({ apiKey, env, preferredModel, region, onMetrics }) -> Promise(clientHandle)
   - Validates API key, fetches small capability manifest (models + streaming support), warms any required token cache.
   - onMetrics is optional callback; receives a single object per request finish with {route, model, latency_ms, status}.

2) client.generate({ prompt, maxTokens, temperature, metadata }) -> Promise({ id, text, tokensUsed })\   - Simple one-shot generation. metadata is opaque string for customer correlation (e.g., session_id).

3) client.streamChat({ messages, onDelta, onComplete, onError, metadata }) -> CancelToken\   - Returns a cancel token. onDelta called with partial text chunks and structured deltas when function-calling is used.

4) client.shutdown() -> Promise<void)\   - Graceful shutdown, flush telemetry, close any streaming sockets.

Additional helpers:
- client.embedBatch(texts[]) -> Promise(embeddingMatrix)\- small convenience wrappers for common UX patterns (summarizeFirstK, rerank) as optional plugins, not core.

Protoflow: "10-minute happy path" (developer guide flow)
1) Install: npm i @redwood/inference-thin (or yarn)
   - Note in README: include a one-line web snippet for CDN usage for quick demos.
2) Bootstrap: add rwinf.bootstrap({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY, env: "hosted" }) in app init code.
3) Send: call client.generate(...) from button handler; show a loading skeleton.
4) Stream: switch to streamChat for conversational demos (UI appends onDelta chunks).
5) Observe: hook optional onMetrics to a simple console.log; show query/latency in a corner badge.
6) Tear down: call shutdown on component unmount.

CLI-first quickstart (dev loop)
- rwinf init --mode=demo --seed-prompt="Summarize the following..."\  - creates .rwinf/config.json, example app js, and an env.sample with RW_KEY placeholder.
- rwinf run --open -> starts local static server with example UI wired to the SDK, with local stub that proxies to Redwood hosted API.

Example UX patterns and anti-patterns
- Pattern: optimistic UI + streaming increments + finalization token.
- Anti-pattern: baking heavy per-token postprocessing on the client (move to server or background worker).
- Pattern: use metadata to surface customer session ids so SREs can correlate requests in console/trace.
- Anti-pattern: storing raw user content in local storage — suggest ephemeral in-memory cache + optional encrypted local store when required by platform.

Observability & Minimal Telemetry contract
- Emitted events (one per completed request): handshake, request_complete.
- Fields: sdk_version, route, model, latency_ms, success:boolean, error_code(optional), customer_metadata(optional). Keep payload < 1KB.
- Default destination: Redwood hosted telemetry endpoint (redwood-telemetry/v1) with opt-out via config.telemetry = false.

Rollout plan for reference implementation
- Phase 0 (this draft): spec review with eng-dx + applied-ml (2w).
- Phase 1: reference JS thin client + CDN bundle + minimal example app (2 sprints).
- Phase 2: add React/Native templates and a tiny Python wrapper (1 sprint).
- Phase 3: launch samples to docs + cross-link with Console quickstart and Dedicated onboarding guides (1 sprint).

Gating and success metrics (first 90 days)
- 80% of new trial devs can hit the "10-minute happy path" in <10 minutes (measured via guided tour and telemetry opt-in).
- Number of support tickets related to basic onboarding drops by 40% vs current baseline.
- Average first-request latency shown in sample app < 250ms for hosted API from common dev regions.

Open questions / TODOs (notes-to-self):
- Should we include a tiny local simulator to avoid requiring a RW_KEY for early experiments? (pros: lower friction; cons: risk of diverging behaviours).
- Finalize naming: rwinf vs redwoodClient vs RWClient. Leaning to rwinf for short imports.
- Decide default backoff/retry strategy for transient errors (client side): exponential with jitter vs simple linear.
- Decide whether embedded plugins (summarizeFirstK, rerank) live in separate package to keep core surface small.

Implementation pointers for eng team:
- Keep core bootstrap under 500 lines; split streaming and one-shot code paths.
- Use WebSocket fallback for streaming where SSE isn't supported.
- Use adaptive-prefixing: small local KV cache for repeated prompts to reduce token usage.

References and links:
- Confluence: ThinClient protoflows page (linked_artifacts above).
- GitHub prototype: sdk-prototypes/pull/66 (early POC).
- Slack thread: #eng-dx onboarding-shortcuts (see pinned message).

Notes: this is intentionally terse and pragmatic — targets fast dev time-to-first-success. Will expand with code examples and a short video walkthrough once we agree on surface.

Quick action items (next 7 days):
- [Leah] write README boilerplate + minimal example for rwinf.init (in repo)
- [Owen] spike local stub implementation (2d) and share perf notes
- [Maya] draft the CDN build pipeline for single-file bundle
- [Rajiv] add gating metrics to Console team so we can capture first-request funnel

End of draft.
